cases.description: Passing a null Indicator should cause the method to throw a NullPointerException (the CrossedUpIndicatorRule constructor validates its arguments).

When the other indicator is a constant 5 and the NumericIndicator under test is also constant 5, there is no upward crossing at index 0, so the returned rule must be a CrossedUpIndicatorRule and evaluate to false.

Create a NumericIndicator that yields values [2, 4] (e.g., using a ConstantIndicator for 2 and then a custom Indicator that returns 4 at index 1). The other indicator is constant 3. At index 1 the NumericIndicator moves from below 3 to above 3, so the CrossedUpIndicatorRule should be satisfied.

NumericIndicator values are [6, 5, 4]; the other indicator is constant 7. The NumericIndicator never crosses upward over 7, therefore the rule must evaluate to false at any index (here index 2 is tested).

input.value: NumericIndicator that mirrors the same series

cases.expected: instanceof CrossedUpIndicatorRule and rule.isSatisfied(any index) == false
cases.description: When the 'other' indicator is the same instance as the NumericIndicator itself, a crossing cannot occur; the rule should always return false.

NumericIndicator yields values [3, 5, 2, 6] (e.g., via a custom Indicator). The series crosses upward over 4 at index 1 (3→5) and again at index 3 (2→6). The rule must report a satisfied crossing at index 1.
Using the same series as above, at index 2 the NumericIndicator moves from 5 (above 4) to 2 (below 4); no upward crossing occurs, so the rule must be unsatisfied.
Continuing the same series, at index 3 the value rises from 2 (below 4) to 6 (above 4); the rule must be satisfied again.

group: crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - other indicator decreasing while this stays constant

cases.description: NumericIndicator is a constant 5 (via ConstantIndicator). The other indicator decreases from 6 to 4, never falling below 5, therefore no upward crossing can happen at any index.

Even at the last index (2) where the other value is 4 (below 5), the crossing condition requires the NumericIndicator to move from below to above the other; since NumericIndicator never moves, the rule stays unsatisfied.

group: crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - other indicator contains NaN (invalid numeric value)

cases.description: Passing an indicator that returns Num.NaN should cause the CrossedUpIndicatorRule constructor (or its evaluation) to reject the input and throw an IllegalArgumentException.

group: crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - other indicator with same delegate but distinct instance

cases.expected: instanceof CrossedUpIndicatorRule and rule.isSatisfied(any index) == false
cases.description: Both NumericIndicator instances wrap the same underlying delegate (e.g., ClosePriceIndicator). Since they produce identical values at every index, no upward crossing can occur; the rule must always be unsatisfied.

group: crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - other indicator lagging by one bar (offset series)

cases.description: NumericIndicator yields values [1,2,3] (via ConstantIndicator(1) then plus 1 each bar). The other indicator is the same series shifted right by one bar, so at index 0 the other returns null/undefined (treated as below). The NumericIndicator moves from undefined to 1, which is considered an upward crossing, so the rule should be satisfied at index 0.
At index 1 both series have the same value (2). Since there is no transition from below to above, the rule must be unsatisfied.

group: crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - other indicator with mismatched BarSeries

input.value: ConstantIndicator(5) built on a different BarSeries than the NumericIndicator under test

cases.description: The CrossedUpIndicatorRule requires both indicators to belong to the same BarSeries. Supplying an indicator that references a different series should cause the rule construction to throw an IllegalArgumentException.

group: crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - other indicator throws on getValue

input.value: ThrowingIndicator (custom Indicator whose getValue(int) throws RuntimeException("test"))

cases.description: When the rule evaluates isSatisfied(index), it calls getValue on the supplied indicator. If that indicator throws an exception, the same exception should propagate to the caller.

group: crossedOver(Indicator<Num>) - other indicator returns null Num

input.value: NullValueIndicator (custom Indicator that returns null for any index)

cases.description: A Num value of null is not valid for numeric comparisons. The CrossedUpIndicatorRule should detect the null value during evaluation and throw an IllegalArgumentException.
